projects.title: CyberEar Hearing Assistive Technology (HAT) Android Development
projects.description:
Implemented on the Android platform a hearing aid application as a low cost alternative to standard hearing aids.  The app utilizes a hearing test, at standard frequencies an octave apart used by audiologists when characterizing the hearing loss of a patient.  The reported hearing response serves as an audiogram to customize the EQ at these specific bands for each ear individually.  The app was calibrated to the actual output SPL intensity in dB, so that internal RMS calculations on the signal could be compared to real world volume levels.  This was used for both the boost and attenuation on the EQ, as well as for an automatic gain control to protect the user from prolonged periods of use.

The abstract was selected by The Gerontological Society of America for their 67th Annual Scientific Meeting conference.

As advised by Peter Hall, further work is being performed on the app to reduce latency.  The sound engine is being ported to Pure Data (Pd), from the raw DSP engine programed in Java around the Android API android.media classes.  The Pure Data patch is controlled by the app user interface via the libpd and pd-for-android libraries.
